name: Island-wide
description: Events affecting the whole island or not tied to one locality.

name: Fa-Hien Lena (Pahiyangala)
description: Large rock shelter near Bulathsinhala, Kalutara District.

name: Batadomba-lena
description: Rock shelter near Kuruwita, Ratnapura District.

name: Pomparippu
description: Iron Age urn-burial cemetery near the Kala Oya estuary.

stories.title: City of the minister Anuradha
stories.text: The chronicle derives the name from Anuradha, a follower of Vijaya who founded a village here. Pandukabhaya later laid out the royal city with gates, suburbs and quarters for yonas, outcastes and ascetics.

stories.title: The king and the deer
stories.text: Hunting on Missaka mountain, Devanampiya Tissa chased a deer and was met instead by Mahinda. Mahinda tested his intelligence with the riddle of the mango tree before preaching to him.

stories.title: Sela Cetiya and the Ambasthala
stories.text: The Ambasthala dagoba marks the meeting place. The Sela Cetiya on the summit is one of the sixteen great pilgrimage sites.

stories.title: Ancient hospital
stories.text: The ruins below the hill include one of the earliest identified monastic hospitals, with a medicine trough.

name: Tambapanni (traditional landing area)
description: Location is traditional and uncertain; placed in the north-west coastal zone.

stories.title: The first visit
stories.text: Nine months after his enlightenment the Buddha came to the yakkhas gathered here and drove them away. The deity Sumana Saman received a lock of his hair, which was enshrined in the first stupa on the island.

stories.title: The jewelled throne
stories.text: In his fifth year the Buddha came to Nagadipa to settle a war between the naga kings Mahodara and Culodara over a gem-studded throne. Nainativu is also home to the Nagapooshani Amman kovil.

stories.title: The third visit
stories.text: Invited by the naga king Maniakkhika, the Buddha visited Kalyani in his eighth year, then went on to leave his footprint on Sumanakuta.

stories.title: The sea that rose
stories.text: King Kelanitissa wrongly put a monk to death, and the sea flooded the land. To appease it he set his daughter adrift in a golden vessel. She came ashore in Ruhuna and became Viharamahadevi, mother of Dutthagamani.

stories.title: Kotte-period temple
stories.text: The present temple contains celebrated 20th-century murals by Solias Mendis and earlier fabric from the Kotte period.

stories.title: The king in hiding
stories.text: Tradition holds that Vattagamani Abhaya hid in these caves during his exile and turned them into a temple when he regained the throne.

stories.title: Painted caves
stories.text: Five caves with about 150 images and 2,100 m² of murals, mostly repainted under Kirti Sri Rajasinha in the 18th century.

stories.title: Capital of Ruhuna
stories.text: Mahagama was the seat of the Ruhuna princes. Kavantissa and Viharamahadevi raised their son Gamani here.

stories.title: The Tissa Dagoba
stories.text: The great stupa, one of the largest in the south, is attributed to Kavantissa.

stories.title: The written word
stories.text: Here, according to tradition, 500 monks wrote down the Tipitaka and its commentaries on palm leaves. The library was destroyed in the 1848 rebellion and rewriting began afterwards.

stories.title: Thiruketheeswaram
stories.text: One of the five ancient Isvarams of Siva, praised in Tevaram hymns. It stands by the old port of Mantai, was destroyed by the Portuguese, and was rebuilt in the 20th century.

stories.title: "This is all my treasure"
stories.text: When his son Kassapa demanded the royal treasure, the captive Dhatusena led him to Kala Wewa, bathed in its waters and declared that this was all his wealth. He was then killed, walled up alive according to the chronicle.

stories.title: The parricide's rock
stories.text: Kassapa built a palace on the summit of Sihagiri after killing his father. He met his brother Moggallana in battle in 495, and when his elephant turned aside, his army thought he was retreating. Abandoned, he took his own life.

stories.title: The Mirror Wall verses
stories.text: From the 8th to 10th centuries visitors wrote verses on the polished wall, many addressed to the painted women of the frescoes.

stories.title: Pulatthinagara
stories.text: A Chola provincial capital from 1017, it became the Sinhala capital under Vijayabahu I. Parakramabahu I enclosed it with walls, palaces and parks.

stories.title: "Not one drop of rain..."
stories.text: The Culavamsa puts in the king's mouth the maxim that not even a little water from the rain should flow into the sea without being made useful to man. The "sea of Parakrama" joined older tanks into a single great reservoir.

stories.title: Vijayasundararamaya
stories.text: Here Parakramabahu II held a festival for the recovered Tooth Relic; the Vijayasundararamaya temple stands on the site.

stories.title: Stairway of lions
stories.text: Bhuvanekabahu I made this rock his capital and housed the Tooth Relic in the temple at the head of an ornamental stone stairway.

stories.title: Royal capital and temple
stories.text: The capital of the Aryacakravartis was centred on the Kandaswamy temple. The Portuguese destroyed it in 1620, and the present temple was rebuilt under Dutch rule.

stories.title: Sri Pada
stories.text: Buddhists venerate the footprint as the Buddha's, left on his third visit; Hindus attribute it to Siva, and Muslims and many Christians to Adam.

stories.title: Ibn Battuta's climb
stories.text: In 1344 Ibn Battuta climbed the peak by chains fixed into the rock, as pilgrims did before the modern stairways.

stories.title: The fortress of victory
stories.text: Alakesvara built Kotte as a fortress against the Jaffna kingdom; Parakramabahu VI made it the royal capital.

stories.title: The unfinished Berendi Kovil
stories.text: Rajasinha I, who converted to Saivism, began this granite temple. The Portuguese destroyed the city after his death.

stories.title: Sri Dalada Maligawa
stories.text: Vimaladharmasuriya I brought the Tooth Relic to Kandy. The temple was rebuilt by later kings; the octagonal Pattirippuwa was added under Sri Vikrama Rajasinha.

stories.title: The Esala Perahera
stories.text: The great annual procession joins the cults of the four guardian gods with the Tooth Relic, an arrangement attributed to Kirti Sri Rajasinha.

stories.title: Bombing of 1998
stories.text: The temple was damaged by an LTTE truck bomb on 25 January 1998 and later restored.

name: Bellanbandi Palassa
description: Open-air Mesolithic burial site, Ratnapura District.

name: Dambana
description: Present-day centre of a Vedda community near Mahiyangana.

stories.title: Field of small stupas
stories.text: About 60 small coral-stone stupa bases, part of an early Buddhist and urban settlement in the Jaffna peninsula.

name: Godavaya
description: Ancient port near the Walawe estuary, Ambalantota.

name: Samanalawewa
description: Ancient iron-smelting landscape on the southern escarpment.

name: Ritigala
foundedLabel: Traditional 4th c. BCE; monastery 9th c. CE

stories.title: Pandukabhaya's stronghold
stories.text: The young Pandukabhaya fortified himself on Arittha mountain for seven years in his war against his uncles.

stories.title: The forest monks
stories.text: In the 9th century Sena I gave Ritigala to the Pamsukulika ascetics. Its double-platform padhanaghara meditation buildings have no images, in keeping with their austerity.

stories.title: The Avukana Buddha
stories.text: This standing Buddha, about 12 m tall and carved from a single rock face, is popularly attributed to Dhatusena, near his Kala Wewa. Stylistic dating ranges to the 8th-9th century.

stories.title: Rival of the pupil
stories.text: A legend contrasts the master who carved Avukana with his pupil who carved the unfinished Sasseruwa image nearby.

stories.title: Tirukonamalai in the Tevaram
stories.text: The Saiva saint Sambandar praised the temple on Swami Rock in the Tevaram hymns (7th c.).

stories.title: Gokanna and Mahasena
stories.text: The Mahavamsa says Mahasena destroyed a temple of the gods at Gokanna and built a vihara there. Its identification with Koneswaram is debated.

stories.title: Thrown into the sea
stories.text: In 1622-24 the Portuguese under Constantino de Sá de Noronha demolished the temple and used its stones for a fort. Images were later recovered from the sea.

stories.title: The city of the god
stories.text: Devinuwara's great temple of Upulvan/Vishnu was famed throughout the Indian Ocean. Ibn Battuta described its thousand Brahmins and devadasis.

stories.title: Destroyed by the Portuguese
stories.text: In 1587-88 a Portuguese force under Thomé de Sousa sacked the temple.

stories.title: The coming of the Bodhi branch
stories.text: Asoka sent a branch of the Bodhi tree of Bodh Gaya with the nun Sanghamitta. Devanampiya Tissa received it at Jambukola and planted it in the Mahamegha garden, and saplings grown from its seeds were distributed across the island.

stories.title: Oldest historically documented tree?
stories.text: Faxian saw the tree being venerated c. 410 CE. Its continuous history is often cited as making it the oldest human-planted tree with a documented history, though the claim rests on the tradition.

stories.title: A stupa the king did not live to see
stories.text: Dutthagamani started the Great Thupa after his victory. Dying, he was carried on a litter to see the stupa, whose unfinished parts his brother Saddhatissa had covered with white cloth and bamboo.

stories.title: Materials from the earth
stories.text: The chronicle tells how bricks, copper, silver, pearls and gems appeared miraculously across the island for the building.

stories.title: The first stupa
stories.text: At Mahinda's request, the collarbone relic of the Buddha was brought from Asoka's India and Sakka's heaven and enshrined in the island's first stupa. The relic casket's arrival on an elephant marks the founding of relic worship in Lanka.

stories.title: The vatadage
stories.text: The stupa was later surrounded by pillared rings carrying a roof (vatadage), and the stone columns still stand.

stories.title: A nine-storeyed uposatha house
stories.text: Dutthagamani built a nine-storeyed chapter house roofed with copper tiles for the monks. It was rebuilt many times; today 1,600 stone pillars remain.

stories.title: The insult of Giri
stories.text: When Vattagamani fled the Dravidian invaders, a Jain ascetic named Giri jeered at him. Returning to power, the king destroyed Giri's hermitage and built a monastery there, named after himself (Abhaya) and Giri.

stories.title: A rival to the Mahavihara
stories.text: Abhayagiri was open to Mahayana and other currents and was often at odds with the Mahavihara. Faxian counted 5,000 monks there c. 410 CE.

stories.title: Built on the ruins of the Mahavihara's power
stories.text: Mahasena, a supporter of Abhayagiri, built the Jetavana on Mahavihara land. At about 122 m originally, it was among the tallest structures of the ancient world.

stories.title: The forgotten pepper
stories.text: Dutthagamani ate a pepper dish without first offering it to the sangha. As penance he built this stupa where his spear containing a relic had become fixed in the ground.

stories.title: A vatadage stupa
stories.text: Attributed to Vattagamani Abhaya, this small stupa retains rings of pillars from a vatadage roof.

stories.title: Issarasamanarama
stories.text: The chronicle says Devanampiya Tissa built a monastery here for 500 newly ordained noblemen.

stories.title: The Lovers
stories.text: A celebrated Gupta-influenced relief (c. 6th-8th c.) shows a couple, popularly identified with Prince Saliya, son of Dutthagamani, and the low-caste maiden Asokamala, for whom he renounced the throne.

stories.title: Engineering for monks
stories.text: Two stepped bathing pools of the Abhayagiri complex are fed through underground conduits and filtering chambers, a fine example of Anuradhapura-period hydraulic design.

stories.title: The seated Buddha
stories.text: A limestone Buddha in meditation, among the finest examples of early Sri Lankan sculpture. Dating is stylistic and debated.

stories.title: Caves of the merchants
stories.text: A rock-shelter monastery with early Brahmi donative inscriptions. Tradition says it was founded for 500 Vaisya (merchant) converts.

stories.title: The first great tank
stories.text: Attributed by the chronicle to Pandukabhaya at the founding of the city, this is one of the oldest reservoirs in South Asia.

stories.title: Royal tank
stories.text: Attributed to Devanampiya Tissa; it supplied the royal gardens.

stories.title: Where the Buddha meditated
stories.text: The chronicle records that the Buddha rested here in meditation with his disciples on his third visit. The stupa was later associated with Saddhatissa as ruler of Dighavapi.

stories.title: Relics of the third visit
stories.text: Tradition holds that the Buddha visited here on his third journey and that a stupa was raised over relics given to the local ruler. The site's place in the Mahavamsa is debated.

stories.title: The kshatriyas of Kajaragama
stories.text: The chronicle names the princes of Kajaragama among those who attended the planting of the Bodhi tree.

stories.title: Shared sacred ground
stories.text: Kataragama is a pilgrimage site for Buddhists (Kiri Vehera), Hindus (Murugan/Skanda), Muslims (Khidr) and the Vedda.

name: Diva Guhava (location debated)
description: Exact location unknown; placed near Sri Pada.

stories.title: The cave of rest
stories.text: Tradition says the Buddha rested in a cave near Sri Pada after leaving his footprint. Its identification is disputed: candidates include Batatotalena and Kuragala.

stories.title: The monks who moved
stories.text: Tradition holds that Kassapa resettled the monks living at Sigiriya on neighbouring Pidurangala and endowed its monastery, which has early cave inscriptions and a brick reclining Buddha.

stories.title: Hindu form, Buddhist use
stories.text: A stone shrine in South Indian Pallava style with Tantric Buddhist sculpture. It sits near the island's geographic centre and was moved stone by stone when the Bowatenna reservoir was built.

stories.title: A halt of the Bodhi tree
stories.text: Tradition says the Bodhi branch stopped here on its journey from Jambukola to Anuradhapura, and one of its saplings was planted here.

stories.title: Mandalagiri
stories.text: A circular relic house with three rings of slender stone columns on a hill, one of the finest surviving vatadages.

stories.title: Uttararama
stories.text: Parakramabahu I had four great Buddha images carved into a granite face, including a 14 m reclining Buddha. An inscription here records his unification of the sangha.

name: Polonnaruwa Vatadage

stories.title: A house for the Tooth
stories.text: Attributed to Parakramabahu I or Nissanka Malla, it is one of several buildings of the Dalada Maluwa, the Tooth Relic quadrangle.

description: Position aligned to satellite imagery with the in-app Align tool (not surveyed).

stories.title: Nissanka Malla's stupa
stories.text: Its inscriptions credit Nissanka Malla; it is the largest stupa in Polonnaruwa.

stories.title: Chola Hindu temple
stories.text: Built under the Chola occupation, possibly by Rajaraja I's officials; it is the oldest standing structure in Polonnaruwa and carries Tamil inscriptions.

stories.title: Mountain of hermits
stories.text: A rock-shelter monastery with early inscriptions, an important forest-monastery centre in the Polonnaruwa period.

stories.title: A tooth relic of tradition
stories.text: Tradition holds that the stupa enshrines a tooth relic and was built for Princess Somawathi of Ruhuna.

stories.title: Kavantissa's stupa
stories.text: Attributed to Kavantissa, father of Dutthagamani, and said to enshrine a forehead-bone relic.

stories.title: The princess from the sea
stories.text: The golden vessel carrying Kelanitissa's daughter came ashore here. Kavantissa received her and named her Viharamahadevi.

stories.title: A royal wedding
stories.text: Local tradition makes this the place of Kavantissa's marriage to Viharamahadevi.

stories.title: Cittalapabbata
stories.text: A large forest monastery, identified with the Cittalapabbata of the chronicles, in what is now Yala.

stories.title: Where Turnour found the key
stories.text: Tradition says that here George Turnour found the commentary (tika) that unlocked the Pali of the Mahavamsa for his 1837 translation.

stories.title: Prince Aggabodhi's image
stories.text: A standing limestone Buddha about 11 m tall, traditionally attributed to a prince Aggabodhi. It fell and was re-erected in 1991.

stories.title: Mahayana in the south
stories.text: Seven figures carved in relief, including a 15 m Buddha flanked by Avalokitesvara and Tara. They are evidence of Mahayana devotion.

stories.title: Architect from South India
stories.text: Built for Bhuvanekabahu IV, it combines Sinhala and South Indian forms. Its rock inscriptions in Sinhala and Tamil name the builders.

stories.title: Vijayanagara style
stories.text: A stone shrine designed by the South Indian architect Ganesvarachari, showing Dravidian and Vijayanagara influence.

stories.title: Carved wood
stories.text: The drummers' hall of this Kataragama devale is famous for its more than 500 carved wooden panels.

stories.title: Kandyan painting
stories.text: A cave temple begun under Kirti Sri Rajasinha and completed under Rajadhi Rajasinha, with outstanding Kandyan-school jataka murals.

stories.title: The silver of the Mahathupa
stories.text: Tradition says silver ore found here paid for the building of the Ruwanwelisaya, and Dutthagamani founded the temple in gratitude.

stories.title: Forest hermitage
stories.text: A forest monastery with a stone-paved meditation walk (cankamana) and double-platform buildings like those at Ritigala.

stories.title: Parakramabahu's southern seat
stories.text: As ruler of Dakkhinadesa, the young Parakramabahu built Parakramapura here before taking Polonnaruwa.

stories.title: Birthplace of a king
stories.text: The chronicle gives Punkhagama (Dedigama) as the birthplace of Parakramabahu I. A relic chamber excavated at the Kotavehera yielded fine objects now in the site museum.

stories.title: The saint's cave
stories.text: A cave shrine on Kuragala rock associated by Sufi tradition with Abdul Qadir Jilani. The rock also has early Brahmi inscriptions from a Buddhist monastery, and the site has been disputed.

stories.title: First landing
stories.text: Tradition holds that Arab traders landed at Beruwala, making it among the earliest Muslim settlements on the island.

stories.title: Dutch Reformed
stories.text: A cruciform church built by the VOC. Governors, including members of the van Goens family, are buried there.

stories.title: Feast of St Anne
stories.text: A major Catholic pilgrimage site on the Kalpitiya peninsula, linked to the survival of Catholicism under Dutch restrictions.

name: Our Lady of Madhu

stories.title: Flight into the forest
stories.text: Catholics fleeing Dutch persecution at Mantai carried a statue of the Virgin into the Vanni forest, founding the shrine. It has been a refuge for civilians in modern wars.

wiki: Shrine of Our Lady of Madhu

stories.title: Linked to the Ramayana
stories.text: Tradition connects the temple with Rama. It was destroyed by the Portuguese and rebuilt under Kirti Sri Rajasinha.

stories.title: Healing springs
stories.text: One of the five Isvarams, by the Keerimalai springs whose waters were believed to heal, including the mongoose-faced sage Nakula.

stories.title: Pentagonal bastions
stories.text: Built by the Portuguese and rebuilt by the Dutch as one of Asia's largest European forts, it was fought over repeatedly in the civil war.

stories.title: Built of temple stones
stories.text: The Portuguese built the fort with stones from the demolished Koneswaram, and the Dutch and British later held it.

stories.title: After the Matara rebellion
stories.text: The Dutch built this six-pointed fort after Kandyan forces took Matara in 1761.

stories.title: Tomb of Elara?
stories.text: The chronicle says Dutthagamani raised a monument where Elara fell and ordered all to honour it. Paranavitana identified this stupa as that monument, a view most scholars now reject; inscriptions suggest it was built by a minister, Uttara.

stories.title: Finest guardstone
stories.text: The Abhayagiri chapter house has the finest naga-king guardstone of the Anuradhapura period.

stories.title: The moonstone
stories.text: A building in the Abhayagiri complex with the most celebrated sandakada pahana (moonstone), whose concentric bands of animals and lotus are read as an allegory of samsara.

stories.title: Elephant pond
stories.text: A huge rock-cut tank of the Abhayagiri monastery, fed by underground channels from Periyamkulama.

stories.title: Austere meditation houses
stories.text: Double-platform buildings of the Pamsukulika ascetics. They have no images, but their urinals are carved with fine ornament, read as a rejection of luxury.

stories.title: The oldest frontispieces
stories.text: Its four vahalkada frontispieces carry some of the earliest surviving Sinhalese relief sculpture, with Brahmi inscriptions naming donors.

stories.title: Pools of the sacred hill
stories.text: Rock pools of the Mihintale monastery; the Naga Pokuna has a five-headed cobra carved in the rock.

stories.title: Elara's strongest fortress
stories.text: Dutthagamani besieged Vijitapura for four months, the hardest fight of his campaign north. His elephant Kandula broke down its gate.

stories.title: The unfinished colossus
stories.text: A rock-cut standing Buddha, said to be the pupil's rival to the master's image at Avukana. The monastery has early Brahmi cave inscriptions.

stories.title: Mahasena the tank-builder
stories.text: The chronicle credits Mahasena with Manihira (Minneriya) among 16 great tanks. He was later deified locally as "Minneri Deviyo".

stories.title: Aggabodhi II's tank
stories.text: The chronicle credits Aggabodhi II with Gangatalavapi. The dam breached catastrophically in 1986.

stories.title: Girittha
stories.text: Attributed to Aggabodhi II and later enlarged; part of the Polonnaruwa irrigation network.

stories.title: Frontier reservoir
stories.text: A great northern tank with a Buddhist monastery and Tamil merchant-guild inscriptions of the Chola period nearby.

stories.title: The giant canal
stories.text: An 87 km canal carrying water from Kala Wewa to Anuradhapura at a gradient of about 10-20 cm per km, attributed to Dhatusena.

stories.title: Forest of ironwood
stories.text: A forest of na trees (Mesua ferrea) around an ancient forest monastery, beside a rose-quartz ridge.

stories.title: The merchants' hair relics
stories.text: Tradition holds that the merchants Tapassu and Bhalluka, the Buddha's first lay followers, enshrined hair relics here. A Pallava-period inscription and vatadage survive.

stories.title: A Buddhist monastery under Chola patronage
stories.text: Tamil inscriptions call it Rajarajap-perumpalli after Rajaraja I, showing Chola-period support for a Buddhist site and Tamil Buddhism.

stories.title: Landing of the Tooth
stories.text: Tradition says the princess Hemamala and prince Danta landed here with the Tooth Relic, hidden in her hair, after fleeing Kalinga.

stories.title: Seven wells
stories.text: Hindu tradition connects the seven springs with Ravana; Buddhist monastery ruins nearby show early use.

stories.title: The king who gave his head
stories.text: The exiled king Sirisanghabodhi, rather than cause bloodshed, gave his own head to a poor traveller so he could claim the reward offered by the usurper Gothabhaya.

stories.title: Hiding place of the relics
stories.text: Vijayabahu III kept the Tooth and Bowl relics in a temple on Beligala rock before moving them to Dambadeniya.

stories.title: Refuge of princes and relics
stories.text: Later tradition places refuges in the Kotmale hills: the young Gamani's flight to the hill country (Malaya) and the hiding of the Tooth Relic during Magha's rule.

stories.title: House of the Tooth
stories.text: Built by Vijayabahu I for the Tooth Relic. The Velaikkara Tamil inscription recording the mercenaries' oath to protect it stands here.

stories.title: Built in sixty days?
stories.text: Nissanka Malla's Tooth Relic temple. Its name is popularly explained as "built in 60 hours/days", though more likely it refers to the relics housed there.

stories.title: Lotus-stalk columns
stories.text: A small pavilion with stone columns carved like lotus stalks, where Nissanka Malla listened to chanting.

stories.title: Vaulted image house
stories.text: The best-preserved brick gedige, with a corbelled vault in Sinhala-Dravidian style.

stories.title: The great image house
stories.text: A towering brick image house whose walls still rise about 17 m around a headless standing Buddha; Parakramabahu I's Jetavana monastery.

stories.title: White stupa
stories.text: A stupa of the Alahana Parivena still bearing original lime plaster, attributed to Queen Subhadra.

stories.title: Thrice-bent Buddha
stories.text: An image house with the most extensive surviving Polonnaruwa-period murals, showing jatakas and gods.

stories.title: The sage or the king?
stories.text: A rock-cut statue of a bearded man holding a palm-leaf book, popularly identified as Parakramabahu I. Others see a sage such as Pulasti or Kapila. Nearby is a circular library.

stories.title: The unfinished giant
stories.text: Said to have been built by Tamil prisoners of war after Parakramabahu's South Indian campaigns, it would have been the largest stupa in the world but was left unfinished.

stories.title: Stupa of beads
stories.text: Named after the glass beads found on the site and attributed to Queen Rupavati.

stories.title: Pandyan-style temple
stories.text: A stone Siva temple of the 13th century whose fine bronzes are now in the Colombo Museum.

stories.title: Seven storeys
stories.text: The Culavamsa describes a seven-storeyed palace with 1,000 rooms; the massive brick walls still stand.

stories.title: Monastery of the elder Arittha
stories.text: Inscriptions are said to refer to Arittha, who escorted the Bodhi tree; more than 600 ruins lie on the rock.

stories.title: Forest hermitage
stories.text: An ancient monastery on a rock above Ampara, with early cave inscriptions.

stories.title: A rival landing
stories.text: Eastern tradition says Viharamahadevi's vessel came ashore here, not at Kirinda.

stories.title: Two hundred caves
stories.text: A large forest hermitage in the Kumana wilderness, with numerous drip-ledged caves.

stories.title: Start of the pada yatra
stories.text: The pilgrims' foot pilgrimage to Kataragama through Kumana and Yala starts here.

stories.title: East coast Murugan temple
stories.text: An important Murugan temple of the east coast; it was damaged in the 2004 tsunami.

stories.title: The self-manifested lingam
stories.text: A Siva temple of the Batticaloa region with traditions reaching to the Chola period.

stories.title: Rama's arrow
stories.text: Tradition says Rama made the temple tank with an arrow; its annual festival draws pilgrims from across the east.

stories.title: Mahanaga's stupa
stories.text: Attributed to Yatthalayaka Tissa, son of Mahanaga, the founder of the Ruhuna line. It has an elephant wall and a moat.

stories.title: Moon-hill stupa
stories.text: One of the great stupas of ancient Mahagama.

stories.title: God of Kataragama
stories.text: A shrine of Skanda/Murugan, worshipped by Buddhists as Kataragama deviyo. Its Esala festival includes fire-walking and kavadi.

stories.title: Prince Tissa's refuge
stories.text: Tradition links the temple with Prince Saddhatissa during the war between the brothers.

stories.title: The hidden king again
stories.text: Like Dambulla, tradition says Vattagamani took refuge here; an unfinished rock-cut Buddha stands about 12 m high.

stories.title: Giant seated Buddha
stories.text: The temple is known for a 50 m seated Buddha (1970s) and a "hell" tunnel of painted punishments.

stories.title: The poet-monk
stories.text: Totagamuve Sri Rahula, the leading scholar-poet of Parakramabahu VI's reign, taught here. He wrote the Selalihini Sandesaya.

stories.title: A fragment of the Himalaya
stories.text: The Ramayana tradition says Hanuman dropped part of the medicinal mountain here, explaining its unusual flora.

stories.title: Sapling by the river
stories.text: Tradition counts the Kalutara Bodhi among the saplings of the Sri Maha Bodhi. The hollow stupa (1970s) contains a chamber with paintings.

stories.title: God of Sri Pada
stories.text: A shrine of the deity Saman, guardian of Sri Pada. The Portuguese built a church on the site, and the devale was restored under Kandy.

stories.title: The relic in the grinding stone
stories.text: Tradition says the Tooth Relic was hidden from the Portuguese in a grinding stone (kurakkan gala) at this temple before it was taken to Kandy.

stories.title: A king's gift to his mother
stories.text: Parakramabahu VI founded this pirivena in memory of his mother, Queen Sunetra Devi; a slab inscription records the endowment.

stories.title: Oldest building in Kandy
stories.text: A Gampola-period shrine of Natha (Avalokitesvara). Kandyan kings received their royal names here.

stories.title: Seat of the Siyam Nikaya
stories.text: One of the two chapters of the Siyam Nikaya, which share custody of the Tooth Relic temple. Upali Thera from Siam conducted ordinations here.

stories.title: The second chapter
stories.text: The Asgiriya chapter of the Siyam Nikaya, historically linked to forest-dwelling monks.

stories.title: Anuradhapura-period painting
stories.text: A rock-shelter painting of the Buddha in Indra's cave, among the oldest surviving Sri Lankan Buddhist paintings outside Sigiriya.

stories.title: Rajasinha II's refuge
stories.text: Rajasinha II retreated here when Kandy was threatened, and later kings kept a palace. Knox describes the court's movements.

stories.title: Unfinished stone temple
stories.text: Begun under Kirti Sri Rajasinha in a South Indian gopuram-like form and never completed.

stories.title: Relic temple of Gampola
stories.text: Tradition says the Tooth Relic was housed here during the Gampola period; carved stone foundations survive.

stories.title: Kandyan woodwork
stories.text: An image house on 28 carved wooden pillars, typical of Kandyan-era village temples.

stories.title: Hill-country Hindu temple
stories.text: A major Amman temple of the Indian Tamil community, with a towering gopuram.

stories.title: Where the Bodhi tree landed
stories.text: The Bodhi branch arrived by sea at Jambukola, where Devanampiya Tissa waded into the water to receive it. A sapling was planted here.

stories.title: A gold plate from the north
stories.text: A gold-plate inscription found here, dated to the reign of Vasabha, records the founding of a vihara in Nakadiva (Jaffna). It is early evidence of Anuradhapura authority and Buddhism in the north. A Vishnu kovil stands at the site today.

stories.title: Bottomless well
stories.text: A deep natural well that tradition links to Rama.

stories.title: Island outpost
stories.text: Ruined coral-stone fort and horse stables of the Portuguese and Dutch, who bred horses on the island.

stories.title: Guarding the cinnamon and the coast
stories.text: The VOC fort controlled the northwest coast and trade with Kandy through Puttalam.

stories.title: Cinnamon gate
stories.text: Taken by the Dutch from the Portuguese in 1644 and rebuilt. Negombo was the hub of the cinnamon trade.

stories.title: First Dutch foothold
stories.text: The Dutch took it in 1638 in alliance with Rajasinha II, their first conquest on the island.

stories.title: Shrine of all faiths
stories.text: Visited by people of every religion on Tuesdays; it was one of the targets of the 2019 Easter Sunday attacks.

stories.title: Pettah landmark
stories.text: A red-and-white candy-striped mosque built for the Muslim traders of Pettah.

stories.title: Ramanathan's temple
stories.text: Built by Ponnambalam Mudaliyar and rebuilt in granite by Sir Ponnambalam Ramanathan.

stories.title: A temple-museum
stories.text: Founded by Hikkaduwe Sri Sumangala, a leader of the Buddhist revival. It runs the Navam Perahera.
